([[Melbourne, Florida]]) | college = [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] (2004–2008) | draft_year = 2008 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 56 | draft_team = [[Seattle SuperSonics]] | career_start = 2008 | career_end = 2016 | career_position = [[Center (basketball)|Center]] | career_number = 24, 14 | years1 = 2008–2015 | team1 = [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] | years2 = {{nbay|2015|full=y}} | team2 = [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] | years3 = [[2015–16 NBA Development League season|2016]] | team3 = →[[Canton Charge]] | highlights = * [[List of NBA champions|NBA champion]] ([[2016 NBA Finals|2016]]) * 5× [[VTB United League]] champion ([[2009–10 VTB United League|2010]], [[2011–12 VTB United League|2012]]–[[2014–15 VTB United League|2015]]) * 5× [[Russian Professional Basketball League|Russian Professional League]] champion (2009–2013) * [[Russian Basketball Cup|Russian Cup]] winner (2010) * [[VTB United League Defensive Player of the Year]] ([[2013–14 VTB United League|2014]]) * 2× [[VTB United League|All-VTB United League First Team]] ([[2009–10 VTB United League#All Tournament Team|2010]], [[2013–14 VTB United League|2014]]) * [[List of NCAA Men's Division I Basketball champions|NCAA champion]] ([[2008 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2008]]) | bbr = kaunsa01 | medaltemplates = {{MedalSport | Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|RUS}}}} {{MedalOlympic}} {{MedalBronze| [[2012 Summer Olympics|2012 London]]| [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|Team]]}} }} '''Alexander''' "'''Sasha'''" '''Olegovich Kaun''' ({{langx|ru|Александр Олегович Каун}}, born May 8, 1985) is a Russian former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] in the United States for the [[University of Kansas]] for four seasons, where he won an NCAA championship in [[2008 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2008]] before being selected with the 56th overall pick by the [[Seattle SuperSonics]] in the [[2008 NBA draft]]. He played seven seasons in Russia for [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]]. In 2015, he returned to the United States and played his only [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] season with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], where he won an [[2016 NBA Finals|NBA championship]] in 2015–16. In doing so, Kaun became one of the first two Russians in history, along with teammate [[Timofey Mozgov]], to win an NBA championship. He also represented [[Russia men's national basketball team|Russia]] in the [[2012 Summer Olympics]]. ==High school== In high school at the [[Florida Air Academy]], Kaun averaged 13.0 points, 7.0 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], and 2.0 [[Block (basketball)|blocks]] per game as a junior and 15.3 points and 12.6 rebounds per game as a senior. He led his team to a 23–0 record and to the Florida state championships. ==College career== During the fall of 2003, Kaun committed to the [[University of Kansas]]. He also received offers from [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] and [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]]. During his freshman season with the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]], he played in 27 games, starting twice. In his sophomore season he helped the Jayhawks to an 80–68 win against the [[Texas Longhorns]], which made the Jayhawks the 2006 [[Big 12 Conference]] champions. During his senior year, he was the starting center for the Jayhawks and with them he won the [[2008 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2008 NCAA Championship]]. He graduated with a degree in computer science and was selected to the Academic All Big 12 Basketball Team three times, in 2006, 2007, and 2008. ==Professional career== ===CSKA Moscow (2008–2015)=== Kaun was drafted 56th overall in the [[2008 NBA draft]] by the [[Seattle SuperSonics]]. He was the final draft pick in Sonics history, before the franchise moved to [[Oklahoma City Thunder|Oklahoma City]]. His NBA draft rights were then traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] for cash considerations.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/arthur_kaun_080626.html|title=Cavaliers Acquire Draft Rights to Darnell Jackson and Sasha Kaun|date=June 26, 2008|work=NBA.com|access-date=September 9, 2015}} He signed a three-year contract worth [[Euro sign|€]]2,700,000 with the Russian team [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] in 2008.{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/33301/180/cska-signs-terence-morris-sasha-kaun |title=CSKA signs Terence Morris, Sasha Kaun |publisher=Euroleague.net |date=June 22, 2008 }}{{cite web|url=http://kuathletics.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/062408aaa.html |title=Kaun signs with CSKA |publisher=Kuathletics.cstv.com |date=June 24, 2008 }} On May 23, 2012, Kaun re-signed his contract with CSKA, staying three more seasons with the team.{{cite web|title=CSKA re-signs Alexander Kaun|url=http://www.cskabasket.com/news/?id=11189&lang=en|work=cskabasket.com|access-date=August 15, 2013}} In the 2014–15 season, CSKA Moscow has managed to advance to the [[2015 Euroleague Final Four|Euroleague Final Four]] for fourth straight season, after eliminating [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] for the second straight season in the [[2014–15 Euroleague Quarter-finals|quarter-final]] series, 3–1.{{cite news|title=CSKA Moscow routs Panathinaikos to claim Final Four berth|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=246&seasoncode=E2014#!report|access-date=May 18, 2015|work=euroleague.net|date=April 22, 2015}} However, in the semifinal game, despite being dubbed by media as an absolute favorite to advance, once again lost to [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]]. The final score was 70–68, after an Olympiacos comeback in 4th quarter, led by [[Vassilis Spanoulis]].{{cite news|title=Spanoulis comes through again as Olympiacos stuns CSKA|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=249&seasoncode=E2014#!report|access-date=May 18, 2015|work=euroleague.net|date=May 15, 2015}} CSKA Moscow eventually won the third place after defeating [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahçe]] with 86–80.{{cite news|title=CSKA Moscow beats Fenerbahce in third-place game|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=250&seasoncode=E2014#!report|access-date=May 18, 2015|work=eurolague.net|date=May 17, 2015}} In his "contract year", Kaun had the best season since coming in the club, starting in all 30 games played in the Euroleague and averaging a career-high 9.9 points and 4.5 rebounds on 69.1% shooting from the field. After winning his fifth [[2014–15 VTB United League|VTB United League]] championship with CSKA, there were some reports that Kaun had retired from professional basketball.{{cite web|url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article23546938.html|title=Former Kansas center Sasha Kaun retires from pro basketball at the age of 30|publisher=The Kansas City Star|date=June 8, 2015}}{{cite news|title=Sasha Kaun anuncia su retirada|url=http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=113872|access-date=June 9, 2015|work=acb.com|date=June 8, 2015|language=es}} A day later, Kaun denied these reports, adding that he was, however, done playing basketball in Europe.{{cite news|last1=Bedore|first1=Gary|title=Former KU center Sasha Kaun has not retired from professional basketball|url=http://www2.kusports.com/news/2015/jun/09/former-ku-center-sasha-kaun-has-not-retired-profes/?mens_basketball|access-date=June 9, 2015|work=kusports.com|date=June 9, 2015}} ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2015–2016)=== On September 9, 2015, Kaun signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/kaun-signing-2015|title=Cavs Sign Center Sasha Kaun|work=NBA.com|date=September 9, 2015|access-date=September 9, 2015}} He made his debut for the Cavaliers on October 28, recording one rebound, one assist, one steal and one block in a 106–76 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/CLEMEM/gameinfo.html|title=Love leads Cavaliers past Grizzlies 106-76|work=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2015|access-date=February 21, 2016}} Over the first half of the [[2015–16 NBA season|2015–16 season]], Kaun appeared in just nine games for the Cavaliers, scoring a season-high four points on two occasions.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/k/kaunsa01/gamelog/2016/|title=Sasha Kaun 2015-16 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=February 21, 2016}} On April 11, 2016, Kaun was assigned to the [[Canton Charge]], the Cavaliers' [[NBA Development League|D-League]] affiliate,{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/kaun-assign-160411|title=Cavs Assign Sasha Kaun to Canton Charge|work=NBA.com|date=April 11, 2016|access-date=April 11, 2016}} for a day of training.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/recall-kaun-mcrae-160411|title=Cavs Recall Kaun and McRae|work=NBA.com|date=April 11, 2016|access-date=April 11, 2016}} He was reassigned to Canton the next day to help the team in Game 1 of the D-League Eastern Conference Finals against the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/kaun-mcrae-assign-160411|title=Cavaliers Assign Kaun and McRae to Canton Charge|work=NBA.com|date=April 12, 2016|access-date=April 12, 2016}} The next day, he was recalled by the Cavaliers.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/recall-kaun-mcrae-160413|title=Cavs Recall Kaun and McRae - April 13, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=April 13, 2016|access-date=April 13, 2016}} Kaun did not play a single game for the Cavaliers during their playoff run, a run that ended with the Cavaliers defeating the [[Golden State Warriors]] 4–3 in the [[2016 NBA Finals]] to win the championship. Kaun and his teammate, [[Timofey Mozgov]], became the first Russians to win an NBA championship. On July 15, 2016, Kaun was traded, along with cash considerations, to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in exchange for the rights to [[Chukwudiebere Maduabum]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/sixers-complete-trade-cleveland|title=Sixers Complete Trade With Cleveland|work=NBA.com|date=July 15, 2016|access-date=July 15, 2016}} He was waived by the 76ers on July 17,{{cite web|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/blogs/sports/sixers/Sixers-waive-Sasha-Kaun.html|title=Sixers waive Sasha Kaun|work=philly.com|publisher=Philadelphia Media Network|date=July 17, 2016|access-date=July 17, 2016}} and six days later, he announced his retirement from professional basketball.{{cite web|last=Bedore|first=Gary|url=http://www2.kusports.com/news/2016/jul/23/former-jayhawk-kaun-reveals-retirement/|title=Former Jayhawk Kaun reveals retirement|work=kusports.com|date=July 23, 2016|access-date=July 25, 2016}} ==Russian national team== Kaun was a member of the senior [[Russia national basketball team|Russian national basketball team]], and was part of the team that won the bronze medal at the [[2012 Summer Olympics]]. ==Personal life== Kaun is married to Taylor Kaun ([[née]] Blue), a former soccer player at the [[University of Kansas]].Pluto, Terry.
